decisions.quote: The present study reports on a replication of the technical adequacy of the Student Subjective Wellbeing Questionnaire (SSWQ), which is a 16-item self-report instrument for assessing youth’s academic efficacy, educational purpose, joy of learning, and school connectedness, with a sample of adolescents in Grades 6 to 7 ( N = 438).
decisions.reason: Parent source inspection confirms actual empirical programme/scale retest but complete available abstract omits a unique original publication reference/year/finding linkage. Supplied shipped metadata is a plausible identity, not source proof of the actual closest original. The exact-match exclusion is therefore unsupported; no additional missing paper is established either. Preserve actual full-text/reference access limits after attempted acquisition and pending independent reference-enriched mapping, not an administrative exhaustion label.

raw_expert_opinion.quote: The present study reports on a replication of the technical adequacy of the Student Subjective Wellbeing Questionnaire (SSWQ), which is a 16-item self-report instrument for assessing youth’s academic efficacy, educational purpose, joy of learning, and school connectedness, with a sample of adolescents in Grades 6 to 7 ( N = 438).
raw_expert_opinion.reason: The source text is an abstract by Tyler L. Renshaw reporting a replication of the technical adequacy and latent factor structure of the 16-item Student Subjective Wellbeing Questionnaire (SSWQ) in a sample of 438 adolescents. Because only the abstract was available, the blind coder left the original study's bibliographic fields blank. Shipped row input_row_index 712 (Renshaw, Long, & Cook, 2015, 'Assessing adolescents’ positive psychological functioning at school: Development and validation of the Student Subjective Wellbeing Questionnaire.', School Psychology Quarterly, doi: 10.1037/spq0000088) is the original development and validation study of the SSWQ whose psychometric properties are retested here. No prior adjudication or state file exists.
